# Troubleshooting: client can't pay the rest of an invoice
Clients could not pay the rest of a partially paid invoice from the client portal because the Pay now button was hidden.
This is BUG-2210-01 (High). It affected 2.2.1. It was fixed in 2.3.0.

# InvoicePilot Release Notes v2.2.0 "Meridian"
A redesigned client portal, bulk invoice actions, and API v2.
## New Features
- Client Portal 2.0: clients can view invoice history, download statements, and pay online from a single self-serve page.
- Bulk invoice actions: send, remind, or void up to 100 invoices at once from the invoice list.
- API v2 (REST): new endpoints for invoices, customers, and payments with cursor-based pagination.

# Client Portal 2.0 overview
Version 2.2.0 introduced Client Portal 2.0, a single self-serve page where your clients can:
- View their full invoice history
- Download statements
- Pay online
- Accept or decline estimates
Existing portal links from earlier versions keep working with no changes.

# Partial payments
An invoice can be paid in several parts. Each payment lowers the balance, and the status shows Partially paid until the balance is zero.
Clients can pay the remaining balance from the client portal. On 2.2.1 the Pay now button was hidden for partially paid invoices (BUG-2210-01); this was fixed in 2.3.0.
Payment reminders mention the remaining balance, not the original total.

# Welcome to InvoicePilot
InvoicePilot is online invoicing and accounting software for small and mid-sized businesses. You can send invoices, track expenses, reconcile bank accounts, and give clients a self-serve portal.

# Void or delete an invoice
Draft invoices can be deleted. Sent invoices cannot be deleted; void them instead so your records stay complete.
1. Open the invoice.
2. Click More > Void.
3. Enter a reason. The reason is kept with the invoice.
Voided invoices stay in reports with a zero balance and show a VOID watermark.

# Pause or stop a recurring invoice
Open the recurring profile and click Pause. No invoices are generated while it is paused.
When you resume, the next invoice goes out on the next scheduled date. Missed dates are not sent.
To stop for good, click Stop. Invoices already sent are not affected.

# Troubleshooting: reminders sent for voided invoices
Invoices voided with a bulk action kept their scheduled payment reminders, so clients got reminders for void invoices.
This is BUG-2200-03 (Medium). It affected 2.2.0. It was fixed in 2.2.1.

# Note: long invoice workaround for support
For BUG-2310-02, tell customers to send the invoice link. Do not suggest splitting invoices unless the customer asks; it changes their numbering.

# Gap in invoice numbers
Customer: We deleted a draft and now INV-000213 is missing from the sequence. Our auditor asked about it.
Support agent: That's BUG-2000-04: on 2.0.0, deleting a draft uses up its number. It's fixed in 2.0.1. The gap stays, but the Invoice Register report shows the deleted draft for your auditor.
Customer: Got it, thanks.
Linked bug: BUG-2000-04

# Add a new tax rate
1. Go to Settings > Taxes.
2. Click New Tax Rate.
3. Enter a name (for example, NY Sales Tax) and a percentage.
4. Optionally group rates into a tax group, like state plus county.
5. Save. The rate is now available on invoice and estimate line items.
Changing a tax rate only affects new invoices. Existing invoices keep the rate they were created with.

## What to do
- Update to 2.0.1 or later; this happens automatically.
- To fix an old invoice, edit the exchange rate on the invoice and save it.

# Troubleshooting: tax missing on an old draft
Draft invoices that used a tax rate archived later showed an empty tax field instead of the archived rate.
This is BUG-2010-01 (Low). It affected 2.0.1. It was fixed in 2.1.0.

# Changing tax rate changed old invoices?
I was worried, but no, old invoices keep their rate. Only new ones use the new rate.

# Tax summary report
Shows tax collected on invoices and tax paid on expenses for a date range, by tax rate.
Archived tax rates still appear for the periods they were used.

### What happens on the 31st in shorter months?
The invoice goes out on the last day of the month.

# Recurring cadences explained
| Cadence | Example |
| --- | --- |
| Daily | Every day at 06:00 |
| Weekly | Every Monday |
| Monthly | The 1st of every month, or the last day of the month |
| Custom | Every 2 weeks, every 3 months, or every N days |
If a monthly schedule falls on a day that does not exist, like February 30, the invoice goes out on the last day of that month.

### "Can we pay monthly?"
Seats are billed per year. There's no monthly billing.

# Duplicate an invoice
Open an invoice and click More > Duplicate. The copy is a new draft with today's date and the next number.
To bill the same thing every month, set up a recurring invoice instead.

## Fixed in This Release
BUG-2100-02 — Recurring invoices skip a cycle across DST changes
Recurring invoice schedules calculated in local time skipped a billing cycle when daylight-saving time shifted, causing missed invoices for some customers.

# Scan receipts
Added in 2.1.0. Take a photo of a receipt in the mobile app, or upload one, and InvoicePilot extracts the vendor, date, and amount.
## Accuracy
Typed and printed receipts scan reliably. Always check the extracted amount before saving.
> Known issue: BUG-2100-01 (Won't Fix): OCR accuracy on handwritten receipts is below 40%; typed/printed receipts are unaffected. Documented as a known limitation.

# Troubleshooting: scanned receipt is sideways
Receipts photographed in landscape were rotated 90 degrees before OCR, so the amount was often missed.
This is BUG-2100-03 (Low). It affected 2.1.0. It was fixed in 2.1.1.

## Known Issues
| Bug ID | Severity | Status | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| BUG-2100-01 | Low | Won't Fix | OCR accuracy on handwritten receipts is below 40%; typed/printed receipts are unaffected. Documented as a known limitation. |

## Fixed in This Release
BUG-2100-03 — Receipt scanning rotates landscape receipts
Receipts photographed in landscape were rotated 90 degrees before OCR, so the amount was often missed.
BUG-2100-04 — Payment reminder sent twice when the send window crosses midnight
Client-level reminders with a send window that crossed midnight UTC were sent twice.

# Handwritten receipts not scanned
Customer: Receipt scanning doesn't read our handwritten taxi receipts at all.
Support agent: Handwritten receipts are a known limitation, BUG-2100-01 (Low, Won't Fix): OCR accuracy on handwriting is below 40%. Typed and printed receipts scan reliably. Please type the amount for handwritten ones.
Customer: Thanks, that worked.
Linked bug: BUG-2100-01

# Review and confirm suggested matches
Suggested matches show a confidence label: High, Medium, or Low.
- High: amount, date, and reference all match
- Medium: amount and date match
- Low: amount matches only
You can confirm all High matches in one click. Medium and Low matches should be checked one at a time.
Undo a confirmed match from the transaction's history within 30 days.

## How matching works
- Amount must match exactly
- Date must be within 5 days
- Payee or reference text raises confidence
Auto-match runs the first time you open Bank Reconciliation after upgrading. Review suggested matches before confirming them in bulk.
> Known issue: On 2.3.1, auto-match does not convert foreign-currency amounts (BUG-2310-01, Critical). See Multi-currency accounts and bank reconciliation.

## Upgrade Notes
Auto-match runs automatically the first time you open Bank Reconciliation after upgrading; review suggested matches before confirming them in bulk.

# Reconcile transactions manually
Manual reconciliation has been available since 2.0.0 and is still the fallback when auto-match cannot find a match.
1. Go to Banking and open the account.
2. Click an uncategorized transaction.
3. Choose Match to pick an existing invoice or expense, or Categorize to record a new one.
4. When the statement balance and InvoicePilot balance agree, click Finish Reconciliation.

# Bank transactions endpoint
Added to API v2 on 2026-06-15. See the API changelog.

| --- | --- | --- |

| POST | /v2/bank_transactions/{transaction_id}/match | Match a transaction to an invoice or expense |
| POST | /v2/bank_transactions/{transaction_id}/unmatch | Undo a match (within 30 days) |

# Invite users and assign seats
Each person who signs in to InvoicePilot uses one seat. You can invite as many users as you have seats.
1. Go to Settings > Users.
2. Click Invite User and enter their email.
3. Pick a role: Admin, Accountant, Staff, or Read-only.
4. Click Send Invite. The invite link expires after 7 days.
If you run out of seats, an account owner can buy more from Settings > Subscription > Add Seats.

# Users endpoint
Added to API v2 on 2026-07-01. See the API changelog.
| Method | Path | Does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GET | /v2/users | List users and their roles |
| POST | /v2/users/invite | Invite a user. The invite link expires after 7 days |
| PATCH | /v2/users/{user_id} | Change a user's role |
| DELETE | /v2/users/{user_id} | Remove a user and free the seat |
Assigning a custom role through the API needs Enterprise. On other plans, use Admin, Accountant, Staff, or Read-only.

# Enterprise onboarding checklist
1. Kickoff with the named CSM
2. Set up custom roles and invite users (invite links expire after 7 days)
3. Connect bank feeds (unlimited on Enterprise)
4. Set up webhooks (up to 25 endpoints)
5. Review the audit log settings (13 months of history)

# Renewals and license expiry
Every license runs for 12 months from its order date. You can see each license's expiry date under Settings > Subscription.
Licenses renew for another 12 months when you place a Renewal order. We email the account owner 60, 30, and 7 days before expiry.
If a license expires, users on those seats lose sign-in access. Data is kept for 90 days.

# Seats and adding seats
InvoicePilot is billed per seat per year. One seat lets one user sign in.
## Adding seats
Account owners can add seats from Settings > Subscription > Add Seats. Added seats are billed at the plan's full per-seat price and start their own 12-month term from the day you add them. They are not prorated.

# Create your organization
Your organization holds your company profile, base currency, fiscal year, and users.
1. Sign up at app.invoicepilot.example and verify your email.
2. Enter your company name, country, and industry.
3. Choose your base currency. This cannot be changed after your first transaction.
4. Set your fiscal year start month.
5. Choose a plan: Starter, Professional, or Enterprise.

# Exchange rates
InvoicePilot updates exchange rates once a day from a market data provider. You can also enter a rate by hand on any invoice.
Reports convert foreign amounts to your base currency using the rate saved on each transaction.

# Troubleshooting: recurring preview shows the wrong currency
The preview of upcoming recurring invoices showed the base currency symbol for clients billed in another currency. The invoices themselves were correct.
This is BUG-2110-01 (Low). It affected 2.1.1. It was fixed in 2.2.0.

# InvoicePilot Release Notes v2.0.0 "Nova"
A redesigned core app with native multi-currency support.
## New Features
- Multi-currency invoicing: bill customers in their local currency with daily exchange-rate updates.
- New dashboard with at-a-glance revenue, outstanding invoices, and expense trends.
- Redesigned navigation and settings area for faster access to organization preferences.

# Enable multi-currency
Multi-currency invoicing arrived in 2.0.0. It lets you bill customers in their own currency.
1. Go to Settings > Currencies.
2. Turn on Multi-currency.
3. Add the currencies you need.
4. Set each customer's currency on their profile.
> Note: Existing single-currency organizations are not affected until multi-currency is turned on.

# Idempotency error IP-4090
Customer: Our retries fail with 409 IP-4090. We reuse the Idempotency-Key from the first attempt.
Support agent: IP-4090 means the Idempotency-Key was reused with a different request body. Retries must send exactly the same body with the same key. This error is not retryable as-is. If the first request is still running you would get IP-4091 instead, which you can retry after a second.
Customer: That's not great, but we'll use the workaround.

# Error subcodes
> Note: Older integrations that only check the main code keep working: IP-4221 to IP-4226 are all HTTP 422 validation errors.

## Behavior
Same key and same body returns the stored response. Same key and a different body returns 409 IP-4090. A key whose first request is still running returns 409 IP-4091.

# IP-4090 on retry
We got IP-4090 because our retry changed the body (new timestamp field) but kept the same Idempotency-Key. Keep the body identical.

# Authentication
Create an API key under Settings > Developer > API Keys. Send it as a bearer token.
```
curl https://api.invoicepilot.example/v2/invoices \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ip_live_xxxxxxxxxxxx"
```
Keys start with ip_live_ for production and ip_test_ for the sandbox. Keys can be scoped to read-only.

# Sandbox environment
The sandbox is a separate copy of InvoicePilot for testing. Use keys that start with ip_test_.
- Base URL: https://sandbox.api.invoicepilot.example/v2
- Sandbox data is reset on the first day of every month
- Bank feeds in the sandbox use a fake bank called Test Bank with sample transactions
- Rate limits in the sandbox are 60 requests per minute on every plan
- Webhooks fire in the sandbox too

## Set up an endpoint
1. Go to Settings > Developer > Webhooks, or call POST /v2/webhook_endpoints.
2. Enter an HTTPS URL. Plain HTTP URLs are rejected with IP-4226.
3. Choose the events to subscribe to.
4. Copy the signing secret. It starts with whsec_ and is shown once.
Webhooks became generally available on 2026-06-15 for API v2.

# API says IP-4010
Customer: We created a key yesterday and every call returns IP-4010.
Support agent: IP-4010 means the API key is missing or invalid. Check the Authorization: Bearer header. Production needs an ip_live_ key; ip_test_ keys only work in the sandbox.
Customer: Got it, thanks.

# Pitching the API to technical buyers
- REST API v2 with cursor pagination and JSON error codes like IP-4220
- Idempotency-Key on every POST so retries are safe
- Webhooks with HMAC signatures (X-InvoicePilot-Signature)
- SDKs for Python (pip install invoicepilot) and Node.js (@invoicepilot/node)
- Sandbox with ip_test_ keys, reset monthly
API v1 still works with no shutoff date.

# Troubleshooting: report times out on long date ranges
BUG-2300-01: Reports spanning more than 3 years of transactions time out instead of paginating results. Status: Open. Affects 2.3.0 and later.

# Reports endpoint
> Known issue: BUG-2300-01 also affects the API: runs spanning more than 3 years fail. Split the range.

# Client stuck in login loop
Customer: A client on a Mac says the portal sends them back to the login page right after they sign in.
Support agent: That's BUG-2200-01, a Safari login loop caused by a cookie SameSite setting. A fix is already rolling out in 2.2.0. Ask the client to clear cookies for the portal and sign in again.
Customer: That's not great, but we'll use the workaround.
Linked bug: BUG-2200-01

# Note: long invoice workaround for support
For BUG-2310-02, tell customers to send the invoice link. Do not suggest splitting invoices unless the customer asks; it changes their numbering.

## Resolution
Workaround: send by link. A fix to the renderer's pagination is in progress.
## Customer communication
Support linked affected tickets to BUG-2310-02. Customers get an email when the fix ships.

## Root cause
The aggregator had an outage. Our sync retried too fast and was throttled after they recovered.
## Resolution
Added jittered backoff to sync retries. IP-5030 is the correct code for this case and clients should retry with backoff.

# Service status and incidents
Check status.invoicepilot.example for live status. Subscribe to get incident emails.
If the API returns IP-5030 for many requests at once, a bank feed provider is usually down. Check the status page before you open a ticket.

# 503 IP-5030 from bank endpoints
Customer: Since 8am our bank sync gets 503 with IP-5030 on almost every call.
Support agent: IP-5030 means a bank feed provider is unavailable. It is retryable with backoff. We had a provider incident this morning; see status.invoicepilot.example. Your requests should succeed once it recovers.

# Runbook: IP-5030 spike
1. Check the aggregator status dashboard.
2. If the provider is down, post a status page incident.
3. Do not ask customers to change anything. IP-5030 is retryable with backoff.

## Headers
Every v2 response includes:
- X-RateLimit-Limit: your limit per minute
- X-RateLimit-Remaining: requests left in this window
- X-RateLimit-Reset: Unix time when the window resets
When you go over, you get HTTP 429 with error code IP-4290 and a Retry-After header in seconds.
Note: in 2.2.0 these headers were missing (BUG-2200-02). Fixed in 2.3.0.

# Concurrency limits
Besides the per-minute rate limit, each API key can have at most 10 requests in flight at once.
An 11th parallel request gets HTTP 429 with IP-4291 and a Retry-After header. This is different from IP-4290, which means the per-minute limit was reached.
The concurrency limit is the same on every plan. Per-minute limits are 60, 300, or 1,000 by plan.

# ADR-017: Per-key concurrency limit
## Decision
Limit each API key to 10 requests in flight, on every plan. Over the limit returns 429 IP-4291.
## Why
A few integrations ran 50+ parallel workers and caused slowdowns for everyone, while staying under their per-minute limit.

# Classic API
Classic integrations use API v1 at /v1 with page-based pagination: ?page=2&per_page=50.
Errors are plain text messages with no error codes. Rate limit: 30 requests per minute on every plan.

# X-RateLimit-Remaining missing
Customer: We want to back off before hitting limits but v2 responses have no X-RateLimit-* headers.
Support agent: That's BUG-2200-02 (Low): API v2 responses are missing the X-RateLimit-* headers. It's fixed in 2.3.0. Until then, rely on the 429 response and Retry-After.
Linked bug: BUG-2200-02

# InvoicePilot Release Notes v2.3.0 "Aurora"
Automatic bank-reconciliation matching and a custom report builder.
## New Features
- Bank Reconciliation auto-match: connected bank feeds are automatically matched against recorded invoices and expenses.
- Custom Report Builder: build and save reports by combining any combination of accounts, date ranges, and tags.
- Saved report schedules can now be emailed to stakeholders on a recurring basis.

Besides the per-minute rate limit, each API key can have at most 10 requests in flight at once.

The concurrency limit is the same on every plan. Per-minute limits are 60, 300, or 1,000 by plan.

# Webhook retries and failures
Your endpoint must return a 2xx status within 10 seconds. Anything else counts as a failure.
## Retry schedule
Failed deliveries are retried up to 8 times over 24 hours with exponential backoff: after 1 minute, 5 minutes, 30 minutes, 1 hour, 2 hours, 4 hours, 8 hours, and 8 hours.

# ADR-018: Webhook retry schedule
## Decision
Retry failed webhook deliveries up to 8 times over 24 hours (was 5). Disable an endpoint after 3 days of failures.

# Error subcodes
| HTTP | Code | Meaning | Retry? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 404 | IP-4041 | The resource exists but belongs to another organization | No |
| 409 | IP-4091 | A request with this Idempotency-Key is still being processed | Yes, after 1 second |
| 422 | IP-4221 | Line item validation failed (quantity, rate, or tax) | No |
| 422 | IP-4222 | The currency is not enabled for this organization | No |
| 422 | IP-4223 | The customer is archived | No |
| 422 | IP-4224 | The invoice is void and cannot be changed | No |
| 422 | IP-4225 | The estimate is not accepted, so it cannot be converted | No |
| 422 | IP-4226 | Webhook URL must use HTTPS | No |
| 429 | IP-4291 | Too many concurrent requests (more than 10 in flight per key) | Yes, after Retry-After |
| 503 | IP-5031 | Payment processor unavailable | Yes, with backoff |
